propositions: Context-limit escalation on provider-qualified runs (e.g. Bedrock) silently relocates to bare Anthropic model IDs by comparing only ladder constants, never consulting the run's actual model.

The escalation rung target decision in _rung_target ignores the primary model the run is on, so provider-qualified configs produce invalid cross-provider model IDs or unbudgeted spend in container isolation.

models_at_or_above returns bare Anthropic family names instead of preserving provider qualifiers when no model-class table is configured, affecting even the common one-criterion retry before rare deep escalation.
The entry rung fix routed through model-class vocabulary but escalation rungs bypassed it, leaving a second independent code path vulnerable.
Rung targets must be derived from provider agreement between the run's primary model and the class-resolved target, with provider-differing higher rungs dropped rather than crossed.
